projects.name: Desktop-Assistant-
projects.description: A command-line desktop assistant that pairs a local Ollama-hosted language model (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:7b) with a simple agent loop: it takes a natural-language request through a REPL, decides whether it's small talk or an actionable task, and for tasks, has the model generate Python code inside a 'tool block.' The app then executes that code locally, feeds the output back to the model so it can decide whether to continue or finish, and repeats until the task is done. This lets it handle open-ended desktop commands — opening applications, running shell commands, browsing URLs, listing or searching files — without hand-coding a handler for every possible request, making it a small, educational demonstration of a tool-use/reasoning agent loop built entirely on local infrastructure.

projects.name: automailer

Setup involves enabling the Gmail API in Google Cloud, creating an OAuth consent screen, and registering the correct redirect URLs for both the app and the local UI, after which the script authenticates via OAuth and dispatches messages programmatically. It's built as a reusable piece of infrastructure for automated outreach or notification workflows rather than a one-off script.

projects.name: Recommender-Model

As a graded assignment repo it likely covers standard recommender-system techniques — data preprocessing, model training, and evaluation against a benchmark dataset — in the same academic vein as the author's other recommender-systems assignments (NCF, SASRec, TIGER).

projects.name: Transformer-Index-for-Generative-Recommenders
projects.description: A Jupyter Notebook assignment (folder 'tiger_assignment') implementing TIGER — Transformer Index for GEnerative Recommenders — a technique that represents items as discrete semantic ID tokens and uses a transformer decoder to autoregressively generate the next recommended item, rather than scoring a fixed candidate set the way traditional recommenders do. Built as part of a graduate-level recommender systems course.

projects.name: SASrec
projects.description: A from-scratch implementation of SASRec (Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation), built as 'Assignment 2' of a recommender-systems course. It includes a preprocessing script that builds fixed-length user interaction sequences at configurable lengths, a training script (train_sasrec.py) exposing a full set of CLI hyperparameters — batch size, epochs, learning rate, number of transformer blocks/attention heads, dropout, early-stopping patience, device selection (CUDA/MPS/CPU) — plus a dedicated ablation-study runner (run_ablations.sh) that logs results to CSV and a plotting script for visualizing training curves. The thoroughness of the tooling (ablations, plotting, configurable architecture) suggests this went beyond a minimal assignment submission into a small research-style experimentation harness.

projects.name: Neural-Collaborative-Filtering
projects.description: A complete Neural Collaborative Filtering (NCF) pipeline trained and evaluated on the MovieLens 1M dataset, submitted as 'Assignment 1' of a recommender-systems course. The pipeline is split into three stages: data_preprocess.py converts explicit 1-5 star ratings into implicit interactions (rating >= 4 -> positive), performs a 70/15/15 per-user train/val/test split, and injects 4 negative samples per positive interaction; model.py defines a hybrid GMF + MLP NCF architecture trained with binary cross-entropy loss and early stopping on validation loss, checkpointing the best model; and evaluation.py runs Optuna-based hyperparameter search and reports full-ranking Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on the held-out test set, saving both the tuning results and a convergence plot. All scripts auto-detect CUDA and fall back to CPU.

projects.name: Q-Learning
projects.description: A reinforcement-learning coursework repo (folder 'Q-Learning_Tabular_and_Deep-master') implementing both classical tabular Q-learning, which maintains an explicit table of state-action values, and its function-approximation successor, deep Q-learning (DQN), which uses a neural network to estimate Q-values for larger or continuous state spaces - likely benchmarked against the same control environments used elsewhere in the author's RL assignments.

projects.name: AC---Cartpole
projects.description: A reinforcement-learning assignment (folder 'REINFORCE-and-Actor-Critic-on-Cartpole-main') implementing two classic policy-gradient algorithms - REINFORCE (a Monte Carlo policy-gradient method) and Actor-Critic (which adds a learned value function to reduce variance) - both applied to the CartPole balancing control task, likely as a comparative study of the two approaches' sample efficiency and stability.

projects.name: ppo---cartpole
projects.description: A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) implementation for the CartPole environment, structured as train.py (which saves metrics to results/ppo_results.json) and plot_results.py (which automatically overlays PPO's learning curve against prior baseline runs - DQN, A2C, etc. - from earlier assignments if their result JSONs are dropped into the same results folder). This makes it a comparative benchmarking tool across the author's series of RL algorithm implementations on the same control task rather than a standalone PPO demo.

projects.name: Job-Machine
projects.description: A Python-based end-to-end job-search automation pipeline, organized into clearly separated modules: db (persistence layer), intake (resume ingestion/parsing), matching (keyword-overlap scoring between resume content and job postings), discovery (pulling job listings, e.g. via Greenhouse/Lever public APIs or manual CSV import for LinkedIn/Naukri/Indeed), outreach (recruiter contact discovery and templated email generation/sending), pipeline (orchestration tying the stages together), uploads (input file storage), and web (a Flask dashboard for monitoring the whole process). The system was deliberately built to run on SQL Server Express with Windows Authentication and to avoid paid LLM APIs entirely, relying instead on plain-text extraction, keyword matching, and fixed email templates so the whole pipeline can run within free-tier limits.

projects.name: ragnarok-Hackathon
projects.description: A hackathon 'starter baseline' (built to be extended within a 3.5-hour timebox) for a RAG-based AI study assistant that turns raw university course files into a chat-driven study companion. It's structured around three files: app.py, a Streamlit frontend that handles the chat UI and document-loading sidebar; agent.py, the 'brain' that connects to the Groq API and manages prompts to the LLM; and document_parser.py, which extracts and chunks course materials for retrieval. Suggested hackathon extensions included parsing Jupyter notebooks and .mat files, building smarter chunking so the LLM's context window isn't overwhelmed, adding a relevance-search step instead of stuffing the whole course into context, and tailoring the system prompt to act as a quiz-master or flashcard generator - with an explicit hackathon rule to keep the tool aimed at helping students learn rather than answering graded work outright.

projects.name: Self-Driving-Car-Simulation
projects.description: A from-scratch PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) reinforcement-learning engine built with NumPy only - no PyTorch/TensorFlow - including custom Actor-Critic MLPs, manually implemented backpropagation, and Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE), paired with a self-built 2D Pygame physics simulator (car.py, environment.py, map_reader.py). The agent was trained for roughly 15,000 episodes to learn to steer a simulated car around track turns while avoiding collisions, with model.py defining the network, training.json/first.json/second.json/circle.json holding track or run configuration data, and dashboard.py providing a visualization/monitoring layer for training progress.

projects.name: Lecture-Search-Engine

projects.name: Portfolio

projects.name: ProcessDistro
projects.description: An ambitiously-scoped distributed execution framework for LAN environments, written in Rust, that turns a group of local machines into a lightweight computing cluster. A master/controller node splits compute-heavy jobs (matrix multiplication, bulk password hashing, Mandelbrot fractal rendering) into WebAssembly-compilable subtasks and distributes them to edge-node workers, which execute the subtasks inside sandboxed, resource-limited WASM runtimes and report results back. The documented architecture includes dynamic work-stealing for load balancing, automatic fault-tolerant task reassignment, ephemeral-token node authentication, real-time Prometheus-style metrics, and a documented (if partially aspirational) roadmap from basic controller/edge communication through a v1.0 production release - built on tokio for async networking and serde for serialization, with modular controller/, edge_node/, common/, and wasm_tasks/ crates.
